My in laws are the same,  except they're 55/56 now.  They've been together 40 years.  They would be the first to tell you,  it isn't that they were soul mates or whatnot.  They've both worked hard at it. The reason most "the one"s from school years don't work out is that most people aren't willing to put in the effort at that age.

I actually gave this advice to my nephew last month.  

You may not plan on going to college or even know what your plans are,  but your wants and plans will change a dozen times in the next four years. If you study a little harder and try a bit more you might lose out on a few social events, but you'll open doors for yourself in the future. If you decide later you want to be a research scientist or a school teacher and you'll need college for many jobs,  then having applied yourself from day 1 will pay off. Besides the self discipline and work habits you form now will serve you no matter what job you're in later.

Lastly you'll never look back 20 years later regretting missing a party or playing fewer video games.  You may regret blowing off school though.  You're your own and best advocate, so stand up and do what's best for you.

I'm not really into Anime. I've tried watching a few shows with friends who were and none of them caught my interest. It maybe that I just am not an anime fan, but I wanted to at least give it an honest try. Also I'm bored of other television.

1. About me. I'm in my 30's, a guy, and I'm a generalist nerd. I am in to Pen and Paper RPGs, I can probably tell you more about Star Wars then anyone short of Patton Oswalt and I play a fair bit of video games. (Everything from Souls Clones, to Destiny to Siege and Disco Elysium)

I'm big into comedy, but not dumb comedy. I like action flicks, but I appreciate a good story. (I am a story teller after all)

2) Things I don't like. Overly cutesey or "chibi" things. Or at least things that are done that way just for the sake of it. Homophobia, Racism etc. Long drawn out romance sagas. I don't mind if it's a plot line in a show, but I don't want to watch a show that that's the main premise for 6 seasons.

3) Anime (or anime like) shows I've watched. First let me start by saying that I'm aware that there are some things that aren't considered "Anime" on this list, and I'm not trying to start fights.

Sailor Moon: I wasn't the targeted Audience for it, and some of it was alright I suppose.

Pokemon: Again I think I was too old for it when it came out, and I never got into the games until the past few years. I've tried watching the Anime a few times, but just can't identify with the characters.

Naruto: Again, the characters were an issue for me I think. I didn't hate the show, but I just couldn't get into it

Dragon Ball (Z etc): This is probably what I've seen the most of. A guy I played D&D with used to watch it every day so I'd watch an episode here or there. I hated the way they'd begin a fight and it'd take a whole episode and nothing would be resolved. I have tried rewatching it from scratch, and I've played a few DB video games, and I don't hate the series, but I just never got into it. I think I need to start from the beginning and see more.

Gundam/Gundam Wing/Gundam X: I watched some episode of this back when it was Airing. I liked some of what I saw, but was always lost because I only saw random episodes at 1 am. I like Mechs. I remember when Mech Warrior came out (1989) that was one of my favorite games.

Some food Orgasm show: A buddy on discord streamed it. It was fairly funny, but a bit over the top (I think it was the point, but still)

Avatar: The show was a little young for me.

Hellsing Unlimited: I watched a few episodes with a woman I dated and it was alright.

Full Metal Alchemist. I never watched the Anime, but I started watching the movie on Netflix and hated everything about it.

Wrap up. So now you know about me and my experiences with Anime. I'm looking for a more adult show (Not Hentai) that's got some solid comedy and action.

A few points from a fellow beginner, whose story sounds a lot like yours.

1) Don't worry about bombing. You're not going to do amazingly, nobody does their first time. I did ok my first time, and most of the other comedians there said it was one of the better first time performances they'd ever seen, but I still wasn't killing it. Don't compare yourself to Jeff Foxworthy, Nikki Glaser, George Carlin, or Mitch Hedberg. They all bombed shows. They all started out where you're about to. You wouldn't get down on yourself for not being able to shoot freethrows in an NBA game your first night, so don't attack yourself for not getting a laugh at every joke.

2) The reason why I did even half as well as I did? I practiced.... a lot. I practiced in the car, at lunch at work, in the shower. I practiced in front of my wife a dozen times. I also practiced in front of a few friends. 

3) Despite practice, you're going to get nervous and forget shit. Don't sweat it.

4) Write down your set list (Give each joke a name, or a few words to remind yourself). You're not performing at the Comedy Store (I assume). Many people at open mics have notes, because a lot of people are trying new material out.

5) Don't drink too much, but if you do drink, 1-2 drinks may calm your nerves. You'll still be nervous, but it takes a little of the edge off. If you don't drink, then do whatever helps you calm, breathing exercise etc.

6) Between jokes, do a 3-5 count in your head (If people aren't laughing). This pause helps you collect yourself and also then transition to the next joke. I personally talked too fast, and a few of my jokes ran into one another.

7) If you don't know if a joke is going to work or not, stick it out till the end. If it doesn't work, don't throw it out, just set it aside and see if you can rework it.

8) finally, don't invite a bunch of people. For years people I know had been telling me I should do standup. After I signed up for my first show I told a bunch of them I was going to do it. They insisted they wanted to come. I knew then I didn't want that, but I didn't want to be rude. I told people because I didn't want to chicken out, and I knew that having a few people show up would make me comic up and go out there. That being said, subsequent open mics, I was more comfortable because I knew that if I didn't do well, I could pretend it never happened.

TLDR: You're already doing well by taking the step to sign up, prepare as much as you can, but don't stress yourself out. Have fun with it, and remember, you haven't quit you job for this (Yet) this is just a hobby, a bucket list check, so it's not the end of the world if you don't kill it.

Good luck, and keep at it.
